source.title: Illuminating search spaces by mapping elites
source.paraphrase: MAP-Elites organizes solutions by chosen descriptors and retains strong representatives in different cells, exposing variation across a search space rather than only its best overall solution.

research.mechanism_explanation: The paper's descriptor map motivates treating each loaded eligible rotation-feature pair as a separate construction cell. The callback shuffles the cell order with the supplied seed, then cycles through active finite streams, yielding one distinct JSON payload per cell turn. It removes exhausted streams, deduplicates exact canonical payloads, and rejects explicitly supplied depth fields outside 1 through min(6, ctx.depth). This is a coverage-oriented scheduling adaptation, not MAP-Elites: it receives no evaluated fitness feedback and maintains no elite archive. Only the independent evaluator establishes true depth, eligibility, quality and completed cell visits.
research.hypothesis: At the matched completed-call target, balancing proposals across descriptor cells will produce a positive mean paired difference in unique valid cells against synthetic_uniform_pair_selector_v1 across the four development input-seed pairs. Synthetic quality passes are a separate descriptive outcome with no predicted improvement.
research.falsifier: A mean paired unique-valid-cell difference at or below zero across complete matched development comparisons would fail this coverage hypothesis. Any incomplete arm prevents the planned complete-budget comparison and must retain its actual counts. Positive development differences do not establish a generalization result or live trading usefulness.

human_review.summary: The independent development report records complete_equal_calls for all four pairs: each arm completed 4 of 4 calls per run, or 16 per arm in total. In alpha seeds 11 and 29, challenger/reference cell counts were 3/3 and 3/3, with quality passes 2/1 and 1/2. In beta seeds 11 and 29, cells were 3/2 and 4/2, with quality passes 2/2 and 1/2. Coverage differences average +0.75 cells; quality differences are mixed. These are descriptive synthetic observations only, with no held-out results included.
human_review.rationale: Balancing finite streams is a small auditable way to explore the paper-motivated coverage hypothesis without ranking by hidden quality. The implementation is locally authored and uses only the documented test context. The hypothesis is recorded with the result, not claimed as a timestamped preregistration. The reported positive development coverage difference is not evidence that the paper predicts callback superiority. A limitation is that payload fields do not certify evaluator-owned metadata: the evaluator rejected one over-depth challenger proposal in alpha seed 29 and one in beta seed 11 despite the explicit depth-field guard. Those attempts were not completed evaluations, and the callback must not be treated as a certified live depth validator. All quality bits and eligible denominators are fixture-only. Return correlation, live performance and server acceptance remain unobserved; the separate genetic 100,000-simulation target is unmeasured.
